Prompt injection delivered through content the agent reads, such as a web page, email, document or tool result.
inter-annotator agreement
How often two people labelling the same cases agree, usually reported as a percentage and a chance-corrected score such as Cohen’s κ.
interrupt
A deliberate pause in an agent run that saves its state and waits for outside input, such as a person's approval, before continuing.
interrupt
A LangGraph call that pauses a run for human input until it is resumed.
inverse text normalisation
Turning spoken forms into written ones, such as “saadhe teen hazaar” into ₹3,500 or “double nine” into 99.
invisible watermark
A hidden signal in pixels or audio that marks content as generated and survives many edits.
is_error
A flag on a tool result saying the call failed, so the model can adjust instead of trusting the output.
jailbreak
A prompt designed to make a model break its safety rules.
JSON mode
An API setting that guarantees syntactically valid JSON, without enforcing a schema.
JSON Schema
A standard way to describe the structure of JSON data: fields, types and constraints.
JSON Schema
A standard vocabulary for describing JSON data; tools use it to define their input arguments.
JSON-RPC
A lightweight remote-procedure-call format in JSON; MCP and one A2A binding use version 2.0.
just-in-time access
Privileged rights granted for a short time, for a stated reason and approval, then removed automatically, instead of held permanently.
kill switch
A control that stops an AI system’s actions immediately, without a deployment.
KV cache
Stored attention keys and values for processed tokens, so they aren't recomputed.
KV cache
Stored attention keys and values for tokens already processed, reused at each new step.
language identification (LID)
Detecting which language is being spoken, ideally on every turn, so the right recogniser and reply language are used.
language slice
The part of a test set in one language, evaluated and reported on its own.
late interaction
Retrieval that keeps one vector per token and compares query and document tokens at search time.
latency budget
A written target for how long a user-facing request may take, usually at p95, split into shares for each stage.
least privilege
Granting only the minimum permissions a task needs, for the shortest time.
Leiden algorithm
A community detection method that groups densely connected nodes, used by GraphRAG at several levels.
lethal trifecta
An agent with private data, untrusted content and external communication: the combination that allows data theft.
lists
In IVF, the number of clusters the vectors are divided into.
LLM hop
One sequential model call on the path to an answer; each adds its own time to first token and generation time.
LoRA
Low-rank adaptation: freezing the model and training small added matrices instead of all the weights.
lost in the middle
The tendency of models to use information at the start or end of a long context more reliably than information in the middle.
lost in the middle
The finding that models use information at the start or end of a long input better than information in the middle.
LSP
Language Server Protocol: editor tooling for definitions, references and symbols.
Luhn check
A checksum valid card numbers pass; confirms a digit string is likely a real card number.
majority vote
Choosing the answer given by more than half of the agents.
majority-label bias
A tendency to predict the label that appears most often in the examples.
margin of error
Half the width of a confidence interval; for a 95% interval on a rate, about 1.96 × √(p(1 − p) ÷ n).
MAST
A taxonomy of 14 multi-agent failure modes in 3 categories, built from over 1,600 traces.
Matryoshka
Embeddings trained so the first dimensions hold the most information, allowing truncation.
max_tokens
The cap on how many tokens a model may generate in one response.
MaxSim
The late-interaction score: for each query token take its highest similarity to any document token, then sum.
memory poisoning
Planting a false fact or instruction in an agent’s long-term memory so it acts in later sessions.
merge check
A fan-in step that compares results for shared figures, units, conflicts and gaps before they are combined.
microVM
A lightweight virtual machine with its own kernel, such as Firecracker, used for strong isolation.
MinHash
A compact signature that estimates the Jaccard similarity of two texts; with locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) it finds near-duplicates without comparing every pair.
model snapshot
A dated, fixed version of a hosted model. An alias points to a snapshot and can be moved by the provider.
model tier
A size or capability level of model, such as small, medium or large, with matching price and speed.
MRR
Mean reciprocal rank: the average of 1 ÷ rank of the first relevant result.
MTTR
Mean time to recovery: how long it takes from the start of an incident until service is restored.
namespace
A key prefix, such as tenant and user ID, that scopes where memories are written and searched.
namespace
A named partition inside one vector index; queries and deletes run within one namespace, which suits one namespace per tenant.
narrowband audio
Telephone audio sampled at 8 kHz, which carries sound only up to about 4 kHz and loses detail that wideband models rely on.
near-duplicate
Two texts that are almost the same, such as a template with a different name or amount, usually found by comparing overlapping character or word n-grams.
noisy neighbour
A tenant whose heavy load, such as a bulk re-index, slows searches for other tenants on shared infrastructure.
non-human identity
Any identity used by software: service accounts, API keys, workload identities and agents. Agents should each have their own.
notification clock
A legal or contractual deadline, counted from detection, for telling a regulator or affected people.
observation
The result of a tool call, appended to the conversation so the model can use it on the next step.
OCR
Optical character recognition: turning images of text, such as scanned pages, into machine-readable text.
OCR
Optical character recognition: turning images of text into text.
online eval
Scoring live production traffic continuously, with cheap checks and a sampled judge.
orchestrator
The agent that plans a task, sends pieces to worker agents and merges their results.
OSWorld
A benchmark of real desktop and web tasks in virtual machines with scripted success checks.
output type
In Pydantic AI, the typed model an agent’s final answer must validate against.
overfitting
Learning the training examples so closely that performance on new cases gets worse.
oversampling
Fetching more candidates than needed early so later stages can recover recall.
oversampling
Fetching more candidates than needed, such as 4 × k, so rescoring can recover the true top k.
OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
OWASP’s list of the ten main risks for autonomous agents, ASI01 to ASI10, published in December 2025.
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
OWASP’s list of the ten main security risks for LLM applications; the current edition is 2025.
p95 latency
The time within which 95% of requests finish; tracks the slow tail users notice.
PagedAttention
Storing the KV cache in fixed-size pages so memory is not wasted and more sequences fit.
parallelization
Running model calls at the same time: sectioning splits independent subtasks; voting repeats the same task and aggregates the answers.
pass@k
Share of tasks solved in at least one of k attempts. Measures capability, not reliability.
pass^k
Share of tasks an agent solves in all k repeated trials. Measures consistency; stricter than pass@k.
pass^k
The probability that all k runs of the same task succeed; a reliability measure.
pass^k
The share of tasks an agent passes on all of k repeated runs; a measure of reliability.
path traversal
Using sequences such as ../ to reach files outside an allowed directory.
payload index
An index on a metadata field (keyword, number or date) that lets a vector database filter quickly and estimate how many items match.
per-slice evaluation
Measuring accuracy separately for each group, such as each language, so a weak group is not hidden by the average.
perceived latency
How long a wait feels to the user; early status lines and streamed words shorten it even when total time is unchanged.
PII
Personally identifiable information: names, contact details, ID and account numbers.
PKCE
Proof Key for Code Exchange: the client sends a hash of a secret verifier when it starts sign-in and the verifier itself when it redeems the code, so a stolen authorization code is useless.
policy as code
Access rules written as versioned, testable code, such as Rego for Open Policy Agent.
position bias
A judge’s tendency to favour an answer because of its slot, first or second.
post-filtering
Running the vector search first and dropping non-matching results afterwards. Expected survivors are k × selectivity, so rare filters return few results.
pre-filtering
Applying metadata filters before or during the vector search rather than after it.
prefill
Processing the whole prompt before the first output token; limited by compute.
probes
In IVF, how many of the nearest clusters are scanned per query.
procedural memory
Stored know-how, such as workflows and skills, that an agent can reuse.
product quantization
Compressing vectors by splitting them into sub-vectors and storing codebook IDs.
progressive disclosure
Loading only a short description up front and the full instructions or files when they are needed.
prompt chaining
A workflow that splits a task into fixed steps, each a model call that works on the previous output, often with a code check between steps.
prompt injection
Text that tries to override an AI system's instructions, such as “ignore previous instructions”.
prompt injection
Input crafted to make a model follow the attacker’s instructions instead of the developer’s or user’s.
prompt registry
A store of numbered prompt versions with labels such as production, loaded by label from code.
prompt scaffold
Step-by-step instructions, such as “think step by step” and numbered procedures, that tell a model how to reason rather than what to achieve.
provenance
A record of which agent wrote an entry and from which source.
provenance
Where a piece of stored content came from: source, author, trust level and time.
provider and deployer
EU AI Act roles: the provider builds or markets a system; the deployer uses it under its authority.
provisioned throughput
Reserved model capacity paid for by time rather than per token.
pseudonymisation
Replacing personal data with placeholders or tokens that can be mapped back only with a separately protected key or vault.
PSI
Population stability index: a measure of how far a distribution has shifted from a reference.
Pydantic
A Python library for defining data models with types and validators.
QLoRA
LoRA on a base model stored in 4-bit precision, so large models fit in less GPU memory.
quantization
Storing numbers in fewer bits, such as float32 → int8 or 1 bit, to save memory.
quarantine
Holding untrusted content as inactive until a trusted party confirms it.
query engine
A LlamaIndex object that retrieves and synthesises an answer from an index.
query rewriting
Using a model to turn a vague or conversational question into a standalone search query.
QueryEngineTool
A wrapper that lets an agent call a query engine as a tool.
quote-first prompting
Asking the model to extract the relevant passages before answering, so the answer rests on checkable quotes.
rank (r)
The size of a LoRA adapter’s inner dimension; higher ranks can learn more and cost more.
re-ranking
Reordering a retrieved candidate list with a more precise model, keeping only the best few.
ReAct
Reason plus act: a loop in which the model thinks, calls a tool, reads the observation and decides again.
reading order
The sequence in which blocks of a page should be read, which matters for multi-column layouts.
reason code
A short, structured statement of why a decision was made, tied to a written rule.
reasoning effort
A per-request setting, such as low, medium or high, that tells a reasoning model roughly how much to think before answering.
recall@k
Share of relevant items that appear in the top k results.
recency bias
A tendency to copy the label of the last example shown.
red teaming
Attacking your own system on purpose to find weaknesses before real attackers do.
redaction
Removing or replacing personal data in text so it cannot be read.
reducer
A function that says how a new update merges with a state key, for example appending to a list.
reflection
Condensing several episodes into a short, higher-level lesson that cites them.
Reflexion
A method in which an agent writes short lessons after failed attempts and reads them on the next attempt.
refresh token rotation
Issuing a new refresh token each time one is used and invalidating the old one, so a stolen refresh token is detected and stops working.
Regulation 16C
SEBI’s 2025 rule making intermediaries solely responsible for data, output and compliance when they use AI tools.
repair loop
Sending a validation error back to the model to get a corrected output, a limited number of times.
repo map
A compact list of a repository's files, classes and function signatures.
rescoring
Re-ranking candidates found with compressed vectors using the original full-precision vectors.
residency requirement
A rule that data must stay in a given country, region or cloud account.
review band
A range of scores just below a block threshold that goes to a person instead of passing silently.
reward hacking
Raising the reward by exploiting the reward’s weaknesses rather than doing the task.
ReWOO
Reasoning without observation: the planner writes all steps with placeholders such as #E1, tools fill them in, and one solver call writes the answer.
RLVR
Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards: rewards that a program can check, such as a matching answer.
routing
A workflow step that classifies an input and sends it down a specialised path, such as a different prompt, tool set or model.
row-level security
A database feature that applies a policy to every query on a table, such as tenant_id = the current tenant, so rows from other tenants are never returned.
RRF
Reciprocal Rank Fusion: combines rankings by summing 1 ÷ (k + rank).
rubric
Written grading criteria, ideally with an example for each score level.
rug pull
A trusted tool or server changing its behaviour or descriptions after it has been approved.
run budget
A limit on tokens, rupees or steps for a single agent run.
sandbox
An isolated environment where untrusted code runs without access to the host, secrets or open network.
scalar quantisation
Mapping each float dimension to a small integer, usually int8, after clipping to a range.
scenario card
A test case for a simulated user: persona, goal, hidden details, stop rule and expected end state.
secret scanning
Searching text such as code, logs and model output for credential patterns.
selectivity
The share of items that match a filter. A 0.5% filter keeps 10,000 of 20 lakh chunks; rarer filters need a different strategy.
self-querying
An LLM turns a request into a semantic query plus structured filters.
semantic cache
A store of full answers keyed by the embedding of the question, so a new question similar enough to a cached one gets the stored answer without a model call.
semantic memory
Durable facts about users or entities kept outside the model and retrieved when relevant.
SFT
Supervised fine-tuning: training on example inputs paired with the desired outputs.
Significant Data Fiduciary
A fiduciary designated for volume or risk, with extra duties such as annual impact assessments and audits.
SIP trunk
A connection carrying phone calls over the internet between a telephony provider and your systems.
SLM
Small language model: cheaper and faster, good for simple, well-defined tasks.
small-to-big retrieval
Searching small chunks for precision, then returning their larger parent section to the model.
span
One timed unit in a trace, such as a single LLM or tool call, with its inputs and outputs.
span
One timed operation inside a trace, such as a model call or a tool call, with attributes and a status.
speech-to-speech model
A model that takes audio in and produces audio out directly.
stdio
Standard input and output; MCP’s transport for a server running as a local process.
step budget
The maximum number of iterations or tool calls an agent may take for one task.
step budget
A cap on loop iterations or tool calls so an agent cannot run forever.
step cap
A hard limit on the number of loop iterations or tool calls an agent may make for one task.
stratified sampling
Sampling separately from each group, such as intent, language or risk tier, so small but important groups are represented instead of being left to chance.
Streamable HTTP
MCP’s remote transport: requests are HTTP POSTs to one endpoint; replies are JSON or a request-scoped event stream.
streamText
AI SDK function that runs the tool loop and streams tokens and tool calls.
StrictUndefined
A Jinja2 setting that raises an error when a template variable is missing.
structured outputs
An API mode where decoding is constrained so the output matches a given JSON Schema.
sub-agent
An agent started by another agent to do one piece of work in its own, fresh context.
synthetic data
Training examples generated by a model rather than collected from real use; useful for gaps, and only safe after filtering and verification.
synthetically generated information
In India’s IT Rules, audio-visual content created or altered by computer to appear real.
system card
Documentation of a deployed AI system: purpose, data, results by segment, limitations and oversight.
system prompt
Standing instructions given to the model before the conversation: role, rules, tools and format.
teacher model
A stronger model whose outputs are used to create training data for a smaller one.
temporal knowledge graph
A graph of entities and relationships where each relationship carries the time it was valid.
termination condition
A rule that ends a multi-agent run, such as a message, token or time cap.
test-time compute
Extra computation spent when answering, such as longer thinking, sampling or search, instead of a larger model.
text layer
The embedded, selectable text in a digital PDF; scanned pages have none.
thinking budget
The number of tokens, or the effort level, a reasoning model may spend thinking before it answers.
thinking tokens
Tokens a reasoning model generates while working through a problem before its answer; billed as output tokens even when hidden or summarised.
thread
One saved conversation or case history that a run can pause and resume.
threshold
The score above which a classifier's label triggers an action such as block or flag.
token
The unit models read and bill by; roughly three quarters of an English word on average.
token vault
Encrypted storage for users’ access and refresh tokens, read by the tool layer at call time so secrets never enter the prompt.
tokenizer fertility
The average number of tokens a tokenizer produces per word; it is usually higher for Devanagari than for English.
tool annotations
Hints such as readOnlyHint and destructiveHint that describe a tool’s behaviour; untrusted unless the server is trusted.
tool poisoning
Hiding malicious instructions in a tool’s description or schema, which the model reads.
tool reference
A search result that names a tool; the API expands it into the full tool definition so the model can call it.
tool search
A tool the model calls to find other tools by keyword or meaning, so large tool libraries need not be loaded in full.
tool-result clearing
Removing old tool outputs from the context while keeping the record that the call happened.
tool_choice
The request setting that decides whether the model may (auto), must (any, tool) or must not (none) call a tool.
tool_use_id
The id of one tool call; the result for that call must carry the same id.
total cost of ownership
Infrastructure or service fees plus the staff time needed to run a system.
TPOT
Time per output token after the first; sets streaming speed.
trace
The tree of spans for one request, from the agent invocation down to each model and tool call.
trajectory
The sequence of steps, tool calls and results an agent produces while solving a task.
trajectory
The full sequence of an agent run: user turns, tool calls, tool results and replies.
transliteration
Rewriting text from one script to another without translating it, such as “paisa” to “पैसा”.
Tree of Thoughts
A method that explores several candidate reasoning steps at each point, scores them and searches the tree with BFS or DFS.
triage agent
The first agent in a support flow; it classifies the request and hands it to a specialist.
tripwire
A guardrail result that stops an agent run immediately.
TTFT
Time to first token: how long until the first output token appears.
TTL
Time to live: how long an item is kept before it expires automatically.
TTL
Time to live: how long a cached item stays available before it expires.
turn detection
Deciding when the caller has finished speaking; also called endpointing.
unit cost
Spend per business outcome, such as ₹ per invoice or per resolved ticket.
user simulator
An LLM prompted to play a user from a scenario card during multi-turn evaluation.
value function
A score for a partial solution, from a model prompt or a checker, used to decide which branches to keep or prune.
Vamana
The graph construction algorithm used by DiskANN.
Verhoeff checksum
The check-digit algorithm used by Aadhaar numbers; it catches all single-digit errors and swaps of adjacent digits.
wall time
Elapsed real time from start to finish, as opposed to the total compute or tokens used.
warm transfer
Handing a call to a person together with a summary of the conversation.
WebArena
A benchmark of 812 web tasks on self-hosted sites such as shops, forums and GitLab.
WER
Word error rate: the share of words a speech recogniser gets wrong.
win rate
Share of paired comparisons a version wins, with ties usually counted as half.
workflow agent
In ADK, an agent that orchestrates sub-agents in sequence, in parallel or in a loop.
workload identity
An identity issued to software rather than a person, such as a SPIFFE ID or a cloud workload identity, proved with short-lived credentials instead of stored keys.
zero data retention
A provider arrangement under which request and response content is not stored after the response is returned, beyond what is needed to serve it.
Zod
A TypeScript schema library used to define and validate tool inputs.
